mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in FEDFUNDS exceeds +0.25 percentage points, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive due to anticipation of accommodative monetary policy easing.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day prior period (t-test p > 0.05) during the trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) by more than 2,000 since the previous month is associated with a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return due to labor market tightening and risk-off sentiment.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive in >70% of such labor strength events (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least 3% in HOUST (retail sales) over two months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak demand reduces corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous month * 0.97 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) during the double decline trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by more than 5% from the prior quarter, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to supply-side contraction and reduced investment optimism.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such contraction quarters (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in UNRATE (unemployment) above 4.8% for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 5-day forward return as market anticipates rate hikes and dollar depreciation.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month moving averages are expected to produce a negative S&P 60-day forward return due to dual labor market pressures.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in >80% of such dual-stress events (walk-forward).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in GDPC1 (GDP) growth exceeding +4% from the prior quarter is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as strong demand boosts earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > +4% from prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) during the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS (retail sales) falls below 350 billion dollars during a contractionary regime, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative reflecting weak consumer demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in >60% of such contraction episodes (walk-forward).
